newsitem.title: CHINA: Quotes from China on Deng Xiaoping's death.
newsitem.headline: Quotes from China on Deng Xiaoping's death.

text.p: China's 1.2 billion people bade their last farewell to patriarch Deng Xiaoping on Tuesday with a variety of sayings and expressions of remembrance:
"Comrade Xiaoping's most precious legacy to us is his theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics." -- President Jiang Zemin in his official eulogy.
"We will love you forever" -- silk streamer affixed to funeral wreath from Deng's family.

"Deng gave the economy direction. I wouldn't be in this business if it weren't for him. A few minutes of our time wasn't too much to give." -- Jiang Hui, a Beijing trader of green bean futures after trade halted briefly to mark the memorial.
"My father and mother often tell me never to forget the wise leadership of Comrade Deng Xiaping in raising the living standards of the people." -- 16-year-old Bai Haifeng at his school in Beijing.

"Everybody can see it. The country is richer, the country is stronger. The people are living better lives." -- Zhang Jianming, a 30-year-old high-school teacher from Shaanxi province, watching leaders gather for the official memorial at the Great Hall of the People.

"He was an old man, so he had to die sometime, didn't he? We're thankful for the changes and the progress, but life goes on, doesn't it?" -- 65-year-old Gu Qi, watching the televised ceremonies in Shanghai.

"I don't hold any feelings against him because of (the Tiananmen crackdown in) 1989. I think at the time he made the right decision. Otherwise China might have fallen apart like the Soviet Union." -- a student at Beijing University, hotbed of the 1989 student-led pro-democracy protests.
"China is a society ruled by man not by law... he gave an order and people below him obeyed and the massacre happened.

"Judgment cannot be passed on Deng Xiaoping merely on his contributions and mistakes. Guilt should be added. The June 4 massacre is his guilt not just a mistake." -- Ding Zilin, a university professor whose 17-year-old son was killed in the attack.
"Even if they were giving it away for free, I wouldn't take it." -- taxi driver, when told his passengers were on their way to buy Deng memorabilia.
